title: Neonatal Blood Glucose Trend
scenario: A term infant born to a mother with gestational diabetes is monitored for hypoglycemia in the newborn nursery. Heel-stick glucose is checked serially, with early breastfeeding attempted between checks.

questions.subject: Maternal-Newborn
questions.stem: At which age does the flowsheet show the infant's lowest blood glucose, consistent with neonatal hypoglycemia?
questions.rationale: The 2-hour glucose of 32 mg/dL is the nadir and falls below the 40-45 mg/dL threshold for neonatal hypoglycemia, coinciding with jitteriness, decreased tone, and a poor latch.

questions.subject: Maternal-Newborn
questions.stem: Comparing the later flowsheet entries to the earlier ones, which findings indicate the infant's hypoglycemia is resolving? Select all that apply.
questions.rationale: A glucose climbing above 45 mg/dL, resolution of jitteriness, normalized tone, and successful feeding all show the hypoglycemia is correcting. The temperature never dropped below 36.5 C, so that option does not reflect the trend.
